text:
The board helps developers maintain honest architecture by scanning their code — no model involved — so every solid edge on the screen traces to a real import, call, route, or manifest line. Anything drawn or proposed stays dashed until the scanner finds it in code. The whole thing runs on your machine; nothing leaves it unless you connect a key.

**What it is:** Sequence keeps your architecture honest as the code changes.

**Who it is for:** Developers who want to answer architecture questions from their scanned code, without a model.

**Why it exists:** It reads a repository into a live architecture graph with static analysis and presents that graph beside chat.

**How it works:**
1. A user opens the tool and attaches a repository.
2. The scanner runs static analysis to map services, modules, files, imports, calls, routes, and manifest lines.
3. The scanned graph updates in real time as new code is added or existing code is changed.
4. Questions are answered from the graph; tool-card answers cite file and line references.
5. The architecture board stays current with no external dependencies beyond the repository.

**Advantages:** It answers architecture questions directly from scanned code, runs entirely on the local machine, and traces every edge to real implementation lines — no guessing about what the code actually does.
